For any periodic orbit, an arm whose hub ever becomes zero must thereafter be all-uniform; an always-one hub complements its leaf set, exhausting the two-hub on/off dichotomy. Both always-on yields all nonempty proper subsets independently and precisely R2=(2^a−2)(2^b−2). Exactly one always-on hub forces the other hub through the three-step 0→1→1 clock, with the always-on arm subset size between two and m−2, yielding 3[T(a)+T(b)] period-six labelled states. With neither hub always on both arms synchronize; all sixteen binary-uniform hub/leaf profiles are exhausted in four predicates a≥2,b≥2, giving unique zero fixed point and exactly one three-cycle if both sizes≥2. This establishes no other periods, sharp six onset at max(a,b)=4, and R6/R2=O(2^−a+2^−b) as both grow. Fresh independent whole-state functional graph enumeration for all 25 pairs 1≤a,b≤5 agrees exactly with every formula; the general proof uses uniform-profile reduction, not bounded extrapolation.
